verdict.rationale: Honeycomb's own Triggers and SLO burn alerts are the only documented background automation. Once configured, they evaluate thresholds without user involvement and fire JSON webhooks that can drive downstream integrations, but they only alert and take no autonomous actions. The API's 'automate workflows' is a developer building block, and the MCP server, agent skills and Canvas are interactive, agent-driven investigation; none is shown running autonomously in the background. Missing for 10: autonomous background agents or scheduled AI investigations, automations that take actions beyond alert notifications, user-configurable recurring jobs, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Use triggers to send alerts when thresholds that you define and configure are passed.
Once configured, Honeycomb sends JSON payloads to your webhook upon alerts firing.
This allows you to build custom integrations that receive JSON payloads from Honeycomb upon alerts firing.
